title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context: notes 'Structure à l'infini des M_{g,ν}'. Grothendieck is axiomatizing the combinatorial-analytic 'infrastructure' of the boundary (divisor at infinity) of the Deligne–Mumford compactification, a normal-crossings divisor stratified by stable graphs. On the previous page he introduced a 'catégorie analytique' D, i.e. a category object internal to analytic spaces: D_* is the space of objects, D_** the space of arrows, with source s, target b, identity D_* → D_** and composition on (D_**,b)×_{D_*}(D_**,s). This page finishes the axioms (for every S, the S-valued points form a category) and adds structure. (170) A codimension function c: D_* → N, equivalently (171) D_* = ⊔_d D_d. This induces (172) D_** = ⊔_{d,d'} D_{d,d'}, where (173) D_{d,d'} is the inverse image of D_d × D_{d'} under (s,b): D_** → D_* × D_*. He then imposes three hypotheses (174). a) D_{d,d'} = ∅ if d' > d: an arrow goes from a deeper stratum point to a less deep one, so the target has codimension ≤ that of the source. b) The identity D_* → D_** factors through ⊔ D_d → ⊔ D_{d,d} and induces D_d ≅ D_{d,d}: arrows between points of equal codimension are identities. c) (continued on the next page) For fixed d, the source map D_{d,*} = ⊔_{d'} D_{d,d'} → D_d is a finite covering. It is relatively ordered by factorizability of arrows with given source and graded by d'. It is locally isomorphic to the constant family of posets P(I_d), the subsets of the set I_d of the d local branches of the divisor. Equivalently, it is given by a principal G_d-bundle (monodromy on the branches) over D_d. The left margin correctly notes that b) would follow from c): in P(I_d) the unique element of cardinality d is I_d itself, so D_{d,d} → D_d is an isomorphism. The purpose is an abstract, intrinsic description of the 'structure at infinity': local branch combinatorics plus global monodromy. From it one can reconstruct the stratification category and the stable-graph combinatorics, presumably to study the fundamental-groupoid/Teichmüller tower near infinity. The next page raises the open question whether (s,b): D_{d,d''} → D_d × D_{d''} is a monomorphism, i.e. whether arrows are determined by source and target. He suspects this follows from c).
errors: No mathematical error on this page. Hypothesis b) is redundant given c); Grothendieck himself flags this in the margin.

The monomorphism question raised on the next page is open as stated. For self-intersecting strata it is in general false: a point can map to the same lower-codimension stratum point via two different branches. So arrows need not be determined by source and target. This is exactly why the extra composition data he says must be specified are needed.

ideas.what: Encoding the boundary stratification of a normal-crossings compactification (M_g,ν-bar) as a category object internal to analytic spaces, graded by codimension, with arrows only decreasing codimension and only identities in equal codimension
ideas.modern_name: Category of strata / exit-path category of a stratified space; in the normal-crossings case, the symmetric Δ-complex or generalized cone complex (boundary complex, tropical moduli space)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Exit paths: MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (2000s). Boundary complex of M_g,n-bar as a generalized cone complex: Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne (2015). Symmetric Δ-complexes: Chan–Galatius–Payne (2018–21). Stable-graph category: Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'structure à l'infini' and stratification of M_g,ν by stable graphs, but not, to my knowledge, this internal-category formalism

ideas.what: Local model: for a point of codimension d, the arrows with that source form a covering locally isomorphic to the Boolean poset P(I_d) of subsets of the d local branches, graded by cardinality, with monodromy a principal G_d-bundle
ideas.modern_name: Local structure of a normal-crossings divisor / simple normal crossings stratification; monodromy on branches giving a symmetric (non-simplicial) Δ-complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in toroidal geometry: Kempf–Knudsen–Mumford–Saint-Donat (1973); dual complexes of NC divisors (Danilov, Stepanov, later Payne)

ideas.what: Codimension grading of a category object, with axioms making it 'directed'

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'infrastructure analytique' of the boundary of M_g,ν encodes, as a category internal to analytic spaces, exactly the data later formalized as the generalized cone complex / symmetric Δ-complex boundary complex (tropical moduli space) of M_g,n-bar, including branch monodromy. This was done independently and much earlier than Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne and Chan–Galatius–Payne, and with an analytic (rather than purely combinatorial) object space.
missed.quote: On suppose de plus donnée une fonction "codimension" sur D_* ... D_{d,d'} = ∅ si d'>d ... (une flèche dont source et but sont de même codim, est une identité)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Keeping the strata themselves as analytic spaces of objects, rather than collapsing them to points as tropical geometry does, gives a hybrid object between the stack and its tropicalization. It is close in spirit to Thuillier/ACP skeletons or log-geometric 'Artin fans', and might be of historical and conceptual interest for anabelian approaches to the boundary.

missed.claim: Reconstruction problem: which axioms on the codimension-graded analytic category guarantee that it comes from a normal-crossings compactification, and whether arrows are determined by source and target. This is left open on the next page.
missed.quote: il n'est pas clair ... que les morphismes D_{d,d''} → D_d × D_{d''} sont mono
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor point. The answer (generally not mono, because of self-intersections) is understood in modern treatments via symmetric Δ-complexes.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early, well-conceived abstract axiomatization of the boundary stratification of M_g,ν-bar as an internal category with branch-monodromy local models, anticipating boundary complexes and tropical moduli. But the underlying mathematics is now standard, and this page is setting up definitions rather than proving anything.
transcription_corrections: '(a,b)' in (173) should read '(s,b)' or '(σ,b)', the source/target pair; and 'D_{*,*}' is D_**.
'la but est de codim' should read 'le but est de codim ≤ la codim de la source'.
In b) the index under the second coproduct is 'd ∈ N' (the transcription shows a garbled 'N_ap').
In c) 'b_* ... D_* ⊔ d_*' is a crossed-out attempt; the intended text, continued on the next page, is the source morphism D_{d,*} → D_d.
Top-left margin probably reads: 'c'est-à-dire, ... des strates fermées plus bas...'.
Bottom-left margin reads approximately: 'ce serait conséquence de c) ci-dessous ...', referring to hypothesis b).
